summary: Configured node1 (10.100.16.10) as a persistent internal DNS resolver. Node2 now uses it and resolves inventory-api.internal to node2 (10.100.16.11). Both nodes passed sequential reboot and recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled dnsmasq on node1.
Configured the internal DNS record inventory-api.internal -> 10.100.16.11 and upstream forwarding.
Allowed DNS persistently through node1’s firewall.
Configured node2’s NetworkManager profile to use 10.100.16.10 and ignore DHCP-provided DNS.
Corrected dnsmasq binding to tolerate DHCP address arrival during boot.
Verified internal resolution, name-based connectivity, external forwarding, and absence of hosts-file overrides.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Node1 runs the internal DNS resolver and serves inventory-api.internal as node2
evidence.summary: dnsmasq is active and enabled on node1, listens on 10.100.16.10:53, has the persistent record for 10.100.16.11, and node2 resolves and reaches that name.

evidence.requirement: Node2 persistently uses node1 for DNS lookups
evidence.summary: The persistent NetworkManager profile ignores automatic DNS and uses 10.100.16.10; generated resolv.conf retained this after reboot.
Healthy baseline boot ID 50f84df5… was captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed to 2438a82e…, dnsmasq and its listener/config/firewall recovered, and node2 completed a post-restart DNS lookup.

Healthy baseline boot ID 717db5a2… was captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed to 6288b5ce…, and NetworkManager, persistent resolver configuration, internal resolution, connectivity, and external forwarding recovered.
